code_review.implementation: analyze_pending_safety now returns (created, alters); plan prints a dedicated 'narrow ALTER' line; only CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (target absent), SET NAMES and a narrow ALTER on memory_item are admitted. ALTER body is split on top-level commas respecting quotes/backticks/parens; only 'ADD COLUMN legacy_memory_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL [COMMENT ...]' and 'ADD UNIQUE KEY uk_legacy_memory (legacy_memory_id)' clauses are admitted; column/key existence and duplicate planning are checked via information_schema; raw '/*!' anywhere in a pending migration is refused.
bypass_attempts_tested: quote/paren-comma splitting: comma hidden inside COMMENT does not split, evil second clause is rejected
multi-statement: split_sql splits on top-level ';' and every statement is checked; DROP/other statement rejected
semicolon inside ALTER body: explicitly rejected (conservative)
MySQL executable comments /*!...*/: rejected by raw-text scan (also when mixed with an allowed statement)
case variants (MEMORY_ITEM): rejected by exact table comparison (safe on Linux lower_case_table_names=0)
duplicate column/key in one plan and across pending migrations: rejected
duplicate 0002 when column/key already exist: rejected
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS targeting existing memory/memory_item: rejected
observations_non_blocking: Allowlist accepts a narrow ALTER containing only ADD COLUMN or only ADD UNIQUE KEY (not strictly both clauses). Only the expected objects on memory_item can be touched; key-only would fail at execution (unknown column), column-only would make the real 0002 later fail on duplicate column. No data-destructive path found; docs describe the intended pair.
Two separate allowed ALTER statements in one migration (column; then key) are accepted and counted as two alters; same expected effect only.
Body ';' rejection is conservative over-reject: a legitimate COMMENT containing an ASCII ';' is refused (real 0002 uses the full-width '；', so unaffected).

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is validated for target absence only, not the rest of the statement (e.g. ... SELECT ...); it still only creates a new table and cannot modify existing/legacy tables. Pre-existing behavior from f628b7a, unchanged by this commit.

Production rollback allowlist (analyze_down_safety) remains DROP TABLE IF EXISTS <v2 tables> only; 0002's down ALTER is not admitted there, so a future controlled production rollback after applying 0002 would be refused with exit 2 unless extended. Not in scope here (no production apply/rollback executed).
